name: Khmer

allophone_rules.notes: Khmer consonant letters fall into two registers, the a-series (inherent vowel â [ɑː]) and the o-series (inherent vowel ô [ɔː]). The series is a property of the LETTER, not of the sound it spells: ⟨ក⟩ and ⟨គ⟩ both spell [k] but ⟨កា⟩ is [kaː] and ⟨គា⟩ is [kiə]. Every dependent vowel sign therefore has two readings, chosen by the series of the consonant it is attached to, and the spec gives the a-series reading in the grapheme table and shifts it here. The registers descend from a Middle Khmer voicing contrast that was lost after it had already reshaped the following vowel. The o-series ⟨ា⟩ is the high centring diphthong [iə], the same nucleus ⟨ៀ⟩ spells; Jacob 1968 separates the two by length ([iːə] against [iə]), a distinction this broad transcription does not carry. Source: Huffman 1970, Cambodian System of Writing and Beginning Reader.

Bânták ⟨់⟩, written over the last consonant of a syllable, shortens the nucleus and changes its quality: inherent â [ɑː] becomes [ɑ], inherent ô [ɔː] becomes [u] before a final labial and [ŏə] elsewhere, and the ⟨ា⟩ sign becomes [a] in the a-series and, in the o-series, [ĕə] before a final ⟨ក គ ង ហ⟩ and [ŏə] elsewhere. Source: Huffman 1970.

An initial consonant with no dependent vowel in a weak (unstressed) presyllable is pronounced with its inherent vowel shortened, as if the bânták diacritic were written: a-series â [ɑː] becomes [ɑ] and o-series ô [ɔː] becomes [ŏə]; in casual speech both reduce further to [ə]. Only the final syllable of a Khmer word is strong, so the condition here is that another nucleus follows in the same word. Source: Huffman 1970.

⟨ិ⟩ and ⟨ុ⟩ are [ə]/[ɨ] and [o]/[u] in a closed syllable but [e]/[i] and [o]/[u] closed by a glottal stop in a stressed syllable with no written final consonant. Source: Huffman 1970.

Word-final ⟨រ⟩ rô is silent in the standard (central plains) dialect; Northern Khmer keeps it. Source: Huffman 1970.
Word-final ⟨ស⟩ sâ is [h] (phonetically close to [ç]); Khmer has no final sibilant. Source: Huffman 1970.
The implosives are onset-only: ⟨ដ⟩ dâ and ⟨ឌ⟩ dô are [t] in final position. Source: Huffman 1970.
⟨ប⟩ bâ spells [ɓ] only before a vowel; anywhere else — in a coda or as the head of a cluster — it is [p]. Source: Huffman 1970.
A final ⟨ក⟩/⟨ខ⟩ is a glottal stop rather than [k] after the vowels [ɑː aː iə ɨə uə ɑ a ĕə ŭə] — the short and long low and centring nuclei. After the other vowels it stays [k]. Source: Huffman 1970.

notes: Khmer (Cambodian), written in the Khmer abugida. The spec is organised around the two-series register system: every consonant letter carries an inherent vowel, â [ɑː] for the a-series and ô [ɔː] for the o-series, and that same series decides which of its two readings each dependent vowel sign takes. The grapheme table gives the a-series reading and the allophone rules shift it after an o-series letter. Khmer is not tonal. A word takes at most one final consonant, and finals are unreleased: final ⟨រ⟩ is silent, final ⟨ស⟩ is [h], final ⟨ដ ឌ⟩ are [t], final ⟨ប⟩ is [p], the aspirates lose their aspiration, and final ⟨ក ខ⟩ are a glottal stop after a low or centring nucleus. Three known gaps. A dominant consonant also governs a NON-DOMINANT one later in the same word, across an intervening vowel, and the rules here read only the letter immediately before the vowel sign: ⟨សេរីភាព⟩ is [seːrəjpʰiəp], with the a-series ⟨ី⟩ that the leading ⟨ស⟩ imposes on ⟨រ⟩, and comes out with the o-series [iː] instead. The [ăʔ]/[ĕəʔ] open syllable of Pali and Sanskrit loans is lexically conditioned and not modelled, so ⟨កថា⟩ is [kaʔtʰaː] and comes out [kɑtʰaː]. And the a-series ⟨ូ⟩ is written [oː] here, after Huffman's monophthong table, although both shipped golds transcribe it [ou] — 471 such tokens in the wikipron gold and 183 in ipadict; [ou] is carried as a second candidate rather than promoted, because the spec follows the source and not the gold.

stress.notes: Khmer word stress is predictable and falls on the final syllable of a word or compound; the minor (unstressed) presyllables that precede it are not separately modelled. Stress is not contrastive. Source: Huffman 1970.

ipadict.measured: km/ipadict (n=3261) scores as-scored PER 0.3335 with the harness's own normalize()/levenshtein(), matching the committed board row; the same spec scores 0.1922 against the larger km/wikipron gold (n=6628), and the spec's output for a word attested in both, កក, is kɑːʔ — an exact match to the wikipron gold. Both golds are legitimate: _IPADICT_PROVENANCE["km"] is lexicon-derived, the Khmer-English Dictionary (aakanee.com, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), a human lexicographic source rather than a scrape. Comparing the 1673 words attested in both golds shows the gap is dominated by notational convention, not by a disagreement about Khmer: ipadict doubles the vowel letter for length (kɑɑ) where wikipron and this spec write a length mark (kɑː); ipadict writes v where wikipron and this spec write ʋ; and wikipron and this spec glottalise some final stops (kɑːʔ) that ipadict keeps as a plain stop (kɑɑk). Folding each out of BOTH sides with scripts/fold_km_notation.py: length only 0.2645, glide only 0.3227, final glottal only 0.3353, length+glide 0.2527, all three 0.2510. NEGATIVE RESULT worth keeping: folding the final glottal out entirely makes the row slightly WORSE than as-scored (0.3353 against 0.3335), so that convention is not a removable symbol — the disagreement is about where the mark goes, not whether it is present. A fourth candidate for the residue was checked and not folded: restricted to the 1673 shared words, ipadict marks aspiration at a per-word rate of 0.100 and wikipron at 0.194, while this spec's own output marks it at 0.213, tracking wikipron rather than ipadict. That is consistent with a fourth notational convention, but no reference settles which tradition better reflects the phonetics, so it is reported rather than folded. The three folds above account for roughly a quarter of the raw PER and leave about 0.25 of the row unexplained. This is NOT a case like ki/wikipron or dng/wikipron where folding collapses the row to near zero, and this audit does not claim it is. ENUM CHOICE: none of the closed AuditConclusion values fits cleanly, and this label is chosen for want of a better one. mislabeled_gold is wrong — the gold IS Khmer, correctly labelled. input_limited is wrong — the orthography is not the constraint, since the same spec reaches 0.1922 from the same input against the other gold. at_ceiling_documented would be actively misleading, because it asserts the row cannot meaningfully improve while this audit has just shown a quarter of its error is unaccounted for. change_refused_uncited is recorded because that is literally what happened: the change measured and declined here is retuning the spec toward the ipadict conventions, refused both because no source establishes that transcription tradition as the correct target for Khmer and because it would move the spec away from the larger wikipron gold it currently matches exactly. THIS ROW IS NOT BELIEVED TO BE AT ITS FLOOR: the ~0.25 residue is open work, not a documented ceiling.
